stories.headline: Anthropic says Claude now writes 80%+ of its code, urges global pause as AI nears self-improvement

key_facts.fact: Anthropic Institute published a report 'When AI Builds Itself' on June 4, 2026 saying more than 80% of code merged into its codebase in May 2026 was authored by Claude, up from low single digits before Claude Code launched in February 2025
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic says more than 80% of production code merged into its codebase in May 2026 was authored by Claude. The average Anthropic engineer now merges 8x as much code per day as they did in 2024.

key_facts.fact: The length of tasks AI models can autonomously complete is now doubling roughly every four months, up from an earlier seven-month doubling trend, according to the company's internal data
key_facts.excerpt: The length of tasks that [models] reliably complete on their own has been doubling roughly every four months, up from an earlier trend of doubling every seven months.

key_facts.fact: In a March 2026 poll of 130 Anthropic researchers, the median respondent estimated they produced about four times as much output with Mythos Preview as they would have without access to any AI models
key_facts.excerpt: In a March 2026 poll of 130 employees from across Anthropic research teams, the median respondent estimated they produced around four times as much output with Mythos Preview as they would have without access to any AI models.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic called for a globally coordinated mechanism to slow or temporarily pause frontier AI development; head of policy Jack Clark said some models could be capable of recursive self-improvement within roughly two years
key_facts.excerpt: According to Clark, there's reason to believe that some models could be capable of recursive self-improvement within just two years... a globally coordinated agreement to temporarily pause or at least slow down the pace at which new frontier models are being developed.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic argued any meaningful pause would require multiple frontier labs across different countries, particularly the US and China, plus verification mechanisms to confirm rivals had genuinely stopped
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic argues that any meaningful pause would need to involve multiple frontier AI laboratories operating across different countries. Such an arrangement would also require mechanisms allowing participants to verify that rivals had genuinely stopped developing advanced systems rather than continuing in secret.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic plans to engage lawmakers about recursive self-improvement in the coming months, head of policy Jack Clark said
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic plans to engage lawmakers about recursive self-improvement in the coming months.

stories.headline: Anthropic embeds engineers at NSA to deploy Mythos AI for offensive cyber operations

key_facts.fact: Anthropic has installed about half a dozen forward-deployed engineers inside the US National Security Agency to guide use of its Mythos AI model for offensive cyber operations, the Financial Times reported June 4, 2026
key_facts.excerpt: The San Francisco-based company has installed about half a dozen staff within the NSA as forward-deployed engineers to guide the technology's use and customize models for specific applications, according to Financial Times, citing two people familiar with the arrangement.

key_facts.fact: The deployment comes while Anthropic is suing the Pentagon, which labeled the company a 'supply-chain risk' after Anthropic tried to bar government use of Claude for mass surveillance of American citizens and lethal autonomous drones
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic attempted to limit government use of Claude for mass surveillance of American citizens and lethal autonomous drones, prompting the Pentagon to label the AI lab a 'supply-chain risk.' The company has sued over the designation, which could force it to end contracts with organizations that work with the US military.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic unveiled Claude Mythos in April 2026 to a narrow set of US-based organizations and this week expanded access to 150 organizations across 15 countries
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic recently expanded access to Mythos to 150 organizations across 15 countries.

key_facts.fact: One person close to the situation said Mythos would be useful for infiltrating the networks of nations such as China or Iran; it isn't clear whether Anthropic's engineers are involved in active operations
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic has embedded about half a dozen engineers at the NSA, FT says — It's not clear if the engineers are assisting the NSA in active operations, FT says

key_facts.fact: The model has triggered concern among governments, financial institutions and IT companies over its ability to detect and exploit software vulnerabilities
key_facts.excerpt: The model has triggered concern among governments, financial institutions and IT companies over its ability to detect and exploit software vulnerabilities.

stories.headline: Supabase raises $500M Series F at $10.5B as agents take over database creation

key_facts.fact: Supabase announced a $500 million Series F at a $10.5 billion post-money valuation on June 4, 2026, led by GIC, with Stripe doubling down on a second investment and Salesforce Ventures joining as a new investor
key_facts.excerpt: Supabase, the open source Postgres development platform, today announced a $500 million Series F at a $10.5 billion post-money valuation. The round was led by GIC with all existing investors participating including Accel, Y Combinator, Craft, Felicis, Peak XV, and Coatue. Stripe is doubling down on Supabase with its second investment in the company and Salesforce Ventures joined the round.

key_facts.fact: The round comes seven months after Supabase's Series E and roughly doubles the valuation since October, bringing total capital raised past $1 billion
key_facts.excerpt: The funding comes just seven months after the company's Series E, bringing total capital raised to over $1 billion.

key_facts.fact: Database launches on Supabase grew 600% in the past year, more than 60% of new databases are launched by an AI tool, and Anthropic's Claude Code has been the largest contributor since the start of 2026
key_facts.excerpt: In the past year, database launches on Supabase have grown 600%. More than 60% of new databases are launched by some sort of AI tool... Growth is accelerating since January as Claude Code and Codex expand the number of people who can build.

key_facts.fact: Supabase now has more than 250,000 customers and nearly 10 million developers building on the platform, with 'Supabase for Platforms' recording 370% customer growth in the past six months
key_facts.excerpt: Supabase has over 250,000 customers with many enterprises now turning to Supabase as the backend infrastructure for their AI-native applications... Supabase for Platforms, the product powering most of the top AI app builders, has had 370% customer growth in the past six months.

key_facts.fact: Supabase also released Multigres v0.1 alpha, an open-source 'scalable operating system for Postgres' aimed at providing Vitess-grade horizontal scaling
key_facts.excerpt: Today we're releasing Multigres v0.1 alpha. It's open source and self-hostable... Multigres is a scalable operating system for Postgres that provides high availability and operational simplicity. In a future release it will provide Vitess-grade horizontal scaling.

stories.headline: OpenAI says it will comply with Trump's voluntary pre-release AI model review order

key_facts.fact: George Osborne, OpenAI's head of countries, told CNBC at SXSW London on June 5, 2026 that the company will sign up to the voluntary framework in President Trump's June 2 executive order requiring AI companies to allow federal government assessment of their models before release
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI has told CNBC it will comply with President Trump's AI executive order. George Osborne, Head of OpenAI for Countries, said that the startup would sign up to the voluntary order. Signed by Trump on Tuesday, the order asks for access to AI models 30 days before their release for a benchmarking process to assess their capabilities.

key_facts.fact: Osborne said it is 'quite right that democratic governments have a big role to play in how this technology is used and deployed' and that the company proactively suggested ways for governments to track safety and security issues
key_facts.excerpt: 'It's quite right that democratic governments have a big role to play in how this technology is used and deployed,' he said... 'We proactively suggested ways that governments can keep a track on safety and security issues, not just in the U.S., but more broadly.'

key_facts.fact: The order requests up to 30 days of pre-release access to 'covered frontier models' and a classified benchmarking process led by the NSA Director to assess advanced cyber capabilities; it explicitly does not create a mandatory licensing or preclearance regime
key_facts.excerpt: develop and maintain a classified benchmarking process to assess the advanced cyber capabilities of AI models and determine the threshold at which an AI model should be designated a 'covered frontier model'... provide the Federal Government with access to covered frontier models... for a period of up to 30 days before they plan to release such models to other trusted partners... Nothing in this section shall be construed to [require] the creation of a mandatory governmental [licensing or] preclearance [process] of new AI models

key_facts.fact: OpenAI and Anthropic had previously agreed to share pre-release models with the US AI Safety Institute (CAISI) under the Biden administration in 2024
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI and Anthropic had already agreed to share their models with CAISI back in 2024 under President Joe Biden as part of Biden's push for AI safety guardrails. But until recently, the Trump administration downplayed safety concerns and took a hands-off approach under former White House AI czar David Sacks.

stories.headline: University of Cambridge trials world's first vaccine with key component fully designed by AI

key_facts.fact: Researchers at the University of Cambridge announced on June 4-5, 2026 the first human safety trial of a vaccine whose key component was designed entirely by AI; findings were published in the Journal of Infection
key_facts.excerpt: In what scientists describe as a world first, an artificial intelligence-designed vaccine has successfully completed an initial human safety trial, raising hopes that future vaccines could protect not just against known viruses but also against new variants and even pathogens that have yet to emerge... The findings were published in the Journal of Infection.

key_facts.fact: The team led by Professor Jonathan Heeney fed genetic codes from a range of surveilled coronaviruses into an AI that designed a 'super-antigen' aimed at training the immune system against entire virus families, including mutated and animal-jumping strains
key_facts.excerpt: The Cambridge researchers took known genetic codes – the instruction manuals of life – from a range of coronaviruses that had been recorded by surveillance programmes hunting for potential viral threats. These genetic codes were analysed by an artificial intelligence. It then designed a 'super-antigen' that could train the immune system in such a way it gave protection against the whole family of viruses – even if they mutated or a new infection jumped from animals to people.

key_facts.fact: The first trial involved 39 healthy volunteers and was designed primarily to assess safety; researchers reported no significant safety concerns and immune responses against multiple coronaviruses
key_facts.excerpt: The first human trial involved 39 healthy volunteers and was designed primarily to determine whether the vaccine was safe. Researchers reported no significant safety concerns and found that the vaccine generated immune responses against multiple coronaviruses.

key_facts.fact: A Phase II study with about 200 participants is expected to begin soon to gauge how effectively the vaccine trains the immune system
key_facts.excerpt: A larger Phase II study involving more than 200 participants is expected to begin soon. That trial will focus on determining how effectively the vaccine trains the immune system and whether the broad protection seen in early research can be replicated in a larger population.

key_facts.fact: The Cambridge team is already applying the same technology to develop universal seasonal flu vaccines and an H5N1 bird-flu vaccine; Heeney said the AI's capabilities 'exceeded expectations'
key_facts.excerpt: The Cambridge team are already performing animal research on universal seasonal flu vaccines that would not need to be adapted every year and an H5N1-bird flu vaccine... Heeney said this was the first time an antigen designed by AI had been trialled in people. He said the technology was 'surprising all of us' and it was 'amazing what we can do with it for the good of humanity'.

stories.headline: US officials in talks with AI companies about taking government equity stakes, NOTUS reports

key_facts.fact: Senior Trump administration officials have held preliminary discussions with major AI companies about the federal government acquiring equity stakes in their firms, NOTUS reported June 4, 2026, citing three people familiar with the matter
key_facts.excerpt: Senior U.S. officials have held preliminary discussions with major artificial intelligence companies about the potential for the federal government to acquire some shares in their firms, according to three people familiar with the matter.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman first pitched the concept directly to President Trump in early 2025 and has revisited it with senior administration officials in recent weeks as a way to distribute AI's economic benefits to the public
key_facts.excerpt: Altman first pitched the concept directly to President Donald Trump in a conversation in early 2025, and has discussed it again with senior administration officials in recent weeks as a way to more broadly distribute the economic benefits of AI to the public, they said.

key_facts.fact: Discussions have centered on firms voluntarily ceding shares (not a purchase), with returns potentially directed to public purposes such as a dividend payment to all American households
key_facts.excerpt: discussions have centered on having the firms voluntarily cede the shares to the government, the people said. The returns on the investment could then be directed to public purposes, one of the people said, such as distributing a dividend payment to all American households.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic is not in the discussions with the administration about providing equity stakes, a person familiar with the matter told NOTUS
key_facts.excerpt: No formal agreement is currently in place, and the legal mechanism for any voluntary equity transfer remains unclear. Anthropic is not in these conversations, a person familiar with the matter told NOTUS.

key_facts.fact: The talks come as Anthropic confidentially filed for an IPO with the SEC on June 1 at a reported $965 billion valuation, while OpenAI prepares its own filing, last reportedly valued at $852 billion in March 2026
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic confidentially filed its prospectus with the SEC on June 1 at a reported $965 billion valuation; OpenAI is preparing its own filing, last reportedly valued at $852 billion in March 2026.

key_facts.fact: Sen. Bernie Sanders met Altman this week and plans to introduce legislation that would transfer 50% of the equity in top AI companies to a public sovereign wealth fund and tax their stock at 50%
key_facts.excerpt: Sen. Bernie Sanders called this week for the U.S. government to acquire 50 percent equity stakes in the AI companies, effectively bringing the companies under federal control. The Vermont independent's forthcoming bill also would tax at 50% the stock of OpenAI, Athropic, xAI and other AI firms, with the proceeds being placed in a sovereign wealth fund for the public.

key_facts.fact: The administration in May acquired roughly $2 billion in equity stakes across nine quantum-computing companies, with IBM receiving about $1 billion; Trump earlier converted CHIPS Act grants into a 9.9% stake in Intel
key_facts.excerpt: In May, it announced $2 billion in equity stakes across nine quantum computing companies, with IBM (NYSE: IBM) receiving roughly $1 billion. Trump earlier converted CHIPS Act grants into a 9.9% stake in Intel (Nasdaq: INTC).

stories.headline: Obernolte-Trahan unveil bipartisan AI bill that would preempt state laws for three years

key_facts.fact: Reps. Jay Obernolte (R-Calif.) and Lori Trahan (D-Mass.), with Reps. Erin Houchin (R-Ind.) and Scott Peters (D-Calif.), released a 269-page discussion draft of the 'Great American Artificial Intelligence Act of 2026' on June 4, 2026
key_facts.excerpt: A leading House Republican and Democrat have floated a 269-page discussion draft for a sweeping artificial intelligence bill that would freeze state laws on the topic for three years, and also force the country's most powerful frontier labs to open up their models.

key_facts.fact: The bill would preempt state laws and regulation 'specifically regulating the development' of an AI model for three years; states would keep authority to regulate the use or deployment of AI within their borders
key_facts.excerpt: The bill would preempt state laws and regulation 'specifically regulating the development' of an AI model, with a three-year sunset. The bill specifies that preemption would not apply to laws related to the use or deployment of AI models.

key_facts.fact: Large frontier developers (those with more than $500 million in gross revenue) would be required to publish public AI frameworks covering catastrophic risk, cybersecurity of model weights, critical incident response, and internal misuse mitigations
key_facts.excerpt: The bill would require large frontier developers — those with more than $500 million in gross revenue for the previous calendar year — to establish public frontier AI frameworks. The frameworks would include information on whether a model could pose a 'catastrophic risk,' defined by the bill as 'a foreseeable and material risk' of death or injury of more than 50 people or more than $1 billion in property damage...

key_facts.fact: Developers would retain an Independent Verification Organization licensed by NIST's CAISI for semi-annual audits; they would have to report safety incidents within 15 days and imminent risks within 24 hours
key_facts.excerpt: Large frontier developers would be required to retain an Independent Verification Organization, licensed through the National Institute of Standards and Technology's Center for AI Standards and Innovation. The IVOs would perform semi-annual verification... Developers would be required to report incidents within 15 days of discovery and imminent risks within 24 hours.

key_facts.fact: Critics including Americans for Responsible Innovation and Tech Oversight Project warn the bill replaces a state floor with a federal ceiling, freezing child-safety, civil-rights and consumer-protection laws
key_facts.excerpt: 'The Obernolte-Trahan bill replaces a state floor with a federal ceiling and trades away existing and future child safety, civil rights, and consumer protection laws for nothing in return,' Sacha Haworth, executive director of The Tech Oversight Project, said in a statement to Gizmodo.
